Liers
lī´erz
n. pl. (in the AV only in the phrase liers in wait, an ambush; rendering Hebrew arab)
From lie, to remain in place. The Authorized Version never uses the word alone; liers in wait is its rendering of the Hebrew participle for men set in ambush.

Biblical Definition

Joshua “set the people, even all the host that was on the north of the city, and their liers in wait on the west of the city” against Ai (Jos 8:13), and the men of Ai “wist not that there were liers in ambush against him behind the city” (Jos 8:14). The men of Shechem “set liers in wait for” Abimelech in the mountains (Jdg 9:25). Delilah had “liers in wait abiding in the chamber” while she bound Samson (Jdg 16:12). “Israel set liers in wait round about Gibeah” (Jdg 20:29), and they “came forth out of their places” when the Benjamites were drawn off (Jdg 20:33). Babylon is told, “prepare the liers in wait” (Jer 51:12).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines lier as one who lies down; one who rests or remains; as, a lier in wait or in ambush.

LIER, n. One who lies down; one who rests or remains; as a lier in wait or in ambush.

Key Scripture

Jos 8:13 — "And when they had set the people, even all the host that was on the north of the city, and their liers in wait on the west of the city, Joshua went that night into the midst of the valley."

Jos 8:14 — "And it came to pass, when the king of Ai saw it, that they hasted and rose up early, and the men of the city went out against Israel to battle, he and all his people, at a time appointed, before the plain; but he wist not that there were liers in ambush against him behind the city."

Jdg 16:12 — "Delilah therefore took new ropes, and bound him therewith, and said unto him, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And there were liers in wait abiding in the chamber. And he brake them from off his arms like a thread."

Jdg 20:29 — "And Israel set liers in wait round about Gibeah."

Jer 51:12 — "Set up the standard upon the walls of Babylon, make the watch strong, set up the watchmen, prepare the ambushes: for the LORD hath both devised and done that which he spake against the inhabitants of Babylon."

Modern Corruption

Delilah's liers in wait are read as a story about a strong man's weakness for women, when the text shows a man who knew the ambush was in the room and stayed.

expand to see more

Judges 16 repeats the phrase for a reason. Three times Delilah asks the secret, three times Samson lies, and each time “there were liers in wait abiding in the chamber” and each time she cries, “The Philistines be upon thee, Samson.” He knew. After the first cry he knew there were men behind the curtain; after the second he knew what she was; and he told her the truth the fourth time anyway. The modern reading pities him as a man undone by passion. The chapter shows a man who saw the ambush spring three times and lay down again in the same room, and Proverbs has a name for that: a bird hasting to the snare, and knowing not that it is for his life. Ambush is a fair tactic of war, and Joshua used it at Ai by God's command; it is a fatal tactic of temptation, because the liers in wait only need a man who will not leave the chamber.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew arab (H693), to lie in wait, ambush; oreb (H696), an ambush.

expand to see more

Hebrew arab (H693), participle — liers in wait; Joshua 8:13–14, Judges 9:25, 16:12, 20:29–37, Ezra 8:31.

Hebrew oreb (H696) — an ambush, lier in wait; Jeremiah 51:12.

Usage

"“Their liers in wait on the west of the city” — Ai taken by ambush at God's command."

"“Liers in wait abiding in the chamber” — Samson knew, and stayed."

"“Prepare the liers in wait” — Babylon's fall arranged."
